# Design: A review record per change

## Context

Observed today:

- The review steps exist as roles (`plan.challenge`, `code.review` in
  `codev_core::roles::STEPS`), served by `codev roles`. What they find is
  written nowhere: `assets/workflows/propose.md` step 7 says "Record what
  needs a human decision in the Open Questions of `design.md`", and
  `assets/workflows/apply.md` step 5 keeps notes for the summary only.
- `codev validate <change>` (`codev_engine::validate::validate_change`)
  already checks more than the deltas: the metadata, the roles of
  `change.yaml`, and the proposal's release note and domains
  (`check_proposal`), each check being a pure parser in `codev-core`
  (`changelog::release_note`, `domains`) called by the engine on a file it
  read.
- `codev archive` and `codev sync` refuse any change with a validation
  error: `archive::plan_archive` goes through `sync::plan_sync`, which runs
  the validator first and fails with `validation_failed`.
- Commands taking `--change` share `resolve_change` in
  `codev-cli/src/commands.rs`; every JSON document is a `…V1` type in
  `codev-cli::contract`.
- Reported, not settled here: the skills installed in this repository
  (`.claude/skills/codev-propose/SKILL.md`) were generated by a newer codev
  and already tell the agent to run `codev review` and write `review.md`,
  which this code base has no command or spec for. This change specifies
  that behavior; the record format below is kept compatible with what those
  skills write (headings, `yaml` block fields, statuses), so a record they
  produced is valid.

Constraints: decisions 0001 (functional core, imperative shell), 0002 (the
crate graph is the dependency rule; effects only through ports), 0006
(`serde_norway` for YAML).

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**

- A record format a person reads in a pull request and an agent writes
  with plain file edits, whose defects `codev` locates by line.
- One implementation of the record's checks, used by both
  `codev validate` and `codev review`, so the two never disagree.
- Archive blocked by an unresolved `high` finding with no new gate.

**Non-Goals**

- Commands that write the record (`codev review add`, `answer`…): the
  agent edits the file; validation catches what it gets wrong.
- Detecting a rewritten history: append-only is a rule for the skills,
  checked by people in the diff, not by codev.
- Isolated sub-agent reviewers, a `review:` configuration key, findings of
  `plan.trace`.

## Decisions

### Decision: Markdown with one YAML block per finding

`review.md` is Markdown: `## <step>`, `### <role-id>`,
`#### R-<role-id>-<n> <title>`, then a fenced `yaml` block parsed with
`serde_norway` (decision 0006) into a typed `FindingFields` with
`deny_unknown_fields` off (a future field must not break an older codev
reading a newer record — the same tolerance as the configuration). The
`<!-- codev-review: 1 -->` marker versions the format; a different version
is `review_invalid` rather than a guess.

The heading carries the id and the title so that the record reads as a
document and every issue points at a heading line; the block carries what
must be typed.

**Alternatives considered**: a single `review.yaml` — typed end to end, but
unreadable as a review in a pull request, and a YAML error anywhere loses
the whole file instead of one finding. One file per finding — stable ids
by file name, but scatters a review across dozens of files and makes "what
is open" a directory listing.

### Decision: A pure `review` module in codev-core; the engine resolves locations

Following decisions 0001 and 0002, `codev_core::review` holds, with no I/O:

- `parse(source) -> Parsed<Record>`: steps, roles, findings with their
  line, and the format findings (`review_invalid`, `review_duplicate_id`);
- `Finding::status()` (last history entry), `is_unresolved()`, and
  `waiting_for(&self) -> Option<Party>` (`Author`, `Reviewer`, `Human`),
  implementing the rules of the `review` spec from `raised_by` (or the
  section's role when absent);
- `check_decisions(&Record)`: `review_decision_not_human` and
  `review_unresolved_high`;
- `Location::parse(&str)`: `Code { path, start, end }` or
  `Plan { file, heading }` — a `#` makes a plan location;
- `evidence_matches(evidence, cited_lines) -> bool`: both sides split into
  lines, each trimmed, blank lines dropped; the evidence must appear as a
  contiguous run, each evidence line contained in its target line (a
  quoted fragment of a line is allowed, per the skill's "the fragment that
  matters").

`codev_engine::review` reads `review.md` through the `FileSystem` port,
resolves each unresolved finding's location to its cited text (lines
`start..=end` of the file, or the heading's section of the artifact), and
returns the record plus every issue. `validate_change` calls it next to
`check_proposal`; `codev review` calls the same function.

The plan-location section is found by a heading of any level whose text
equals the location's heading after trimming, and ends at the next heading
of the same or a higher level; the existing `parser::section` only takes
`## ` headings, so it gains a level-agnostic sibling rather than a second
copy of the logic.

**Alternatives considered**: checking the evidence anywhere in the file —
survives line shifts, but a quote that appears elsewhere would "prove" a
wrong location; the reviewer updating a stale location is cheaper than a
proof that proves nothing. Checking evidence in the engine — puts logic
that is pure in the effectful crate, against 0001.

### Decision: The archive gate is a validation error, not an archive rule

`review_unresolved_high` and the other `review_*` codes are `Error`
findings of `codev validate`. The pre-flight in `plan_sync` already
refuses on any error, so `codev archive` and `codev sync` refuse with
`validation_failed` and nothing in `archive.rs` or `sync.rs` changes. It
keeps the property of the `validation` spec: everything archive refuses is
reported upstream by `validate`, with its line.

Consequence accepted: `codev sync` is refused too while a `high` finding is
unresolved. A `high` finding means the change would break a requirement;
merging its deltas into the main specs early is as unwanted as archiving.

**Alternatives considered**: a warning in `validate` plus an archive-only
check — `sync` stays possible, but archive would refuse for a reason
`validate` calls harmless, and skills reading `validation_failed` would
have to learn a second code. Blocking only `high` + confidence `high` —
a reviewer could silence a serious concern by grading it `low` confidence;
a person can still accept or defer it in one history entry.

### Decision: Locations never leave the project

A code location path must be relative, with no `..` component, no root and
no drive prefix (checked lexically in `Location::parse`, so Windows paths
are covered); a plan location's file must be a plain file name or a path
under the change folder with the same rules. Anything else is
`review_location_not_found` without any read. The engine then reads only
`layout.project_root().join(path)`.

**Alternatives considered**: canonicalizing and comparing prefixes —
needs the real filesystem in the core and behaves differently on Windows;
the lexical rule is simpler and enough, since codev only compares the text
and never prints it.

### Decision: `codev review` is read-only and exits 0 on issues

`codev review [--change] [--json]` resolves the change with the shared
`resolve_change`, calls the engine use case, and renders. Its JSON is a new
`ReviewReportV1` in `codev-cli::contract` (with `ReviewFindingV1`,
`ReviewHistoryEntryV1`), mapped from the engine's types, never derived from
them; issues reuse the finding shape of `ValidateReportV1`. It exits 0 when
it read the change: it is the place to look, `validate` is the gate.

**Alternatives considered**: a `--strict` flag failing on issues — the
gate already exists (`codev validate`), a second one would drift.

### Decision: The skills share one review-record block

The record's rules for an agent (format, the severity and confidence
scales, grading with evidence, what is not a finding, author answer,
single re-check, only a person decides a risk, check with `codev review`,
report from the record) live in one asset,
`assets/workflows/_review-record.md`, included in both `propose.md` step 7
and `apply.md` step 5, the way `_update-notice.md` is shared. The scales
are written once there and in the docs; a `codev-agents` test checks both
generated bodies carry them.

**Alternatives considered**: serving the scales through `codev roles` —
a contract change for text that only the two skills read.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [A location goes stale when other fixes shift the lines of an open
  finding, failing validation] → the issue names the finding and its
  location; the skill's "check the record" step fixes locations before
  reporting, and resolved findings are never checked.
- [An agent rewrites a history entry instead of appending] → not
  detectable by codev; the skill text forbids it and the record lives in
  the pull request diff, where a rewrite is visible.
- [A YAML pitfall — an unquoted `location` holding `: `] → one finding is
  `review_invalid` with its line, the others still parse; the skill tells
  the agent to quote locations.
- [`codev sync` is refused for an open `high` finding, surprising a user
  who syncs mid-change] → the `validation_failed` message points to
  `codev validate`, whose error says how to resolve the finding.
- [A symlink inside the project pointing outside] → codev reads it only to
  compare text and never outputs the content; accepted.

## Migration Plan

No data migration: no existing change holds a `review.md`, archived
changes are never checked, and the JSON contract only gains a new report.
Skills pick up the new steps through `codev update`. Rollback: revert the
release; existing `review.md` files are inert Markdown for an older codev.

## Open Questions

None that changes the specs. Assumptions made without a user to ask:

- `codev sync` is blocked like `codev archive` by an unresolved `high`
  finding (see the archive-gate decision).
- A `high` finding blocks whatever its confidence.
- `codev review` has no write subcommands in this change.

# Proposal: A review record per change

## Why

What the reviewers find — the skeptic and the experts at `plan.challenge`,
the newcomer and the experts at `code.review` — lives only in the
conversation: a finding cites no verifiable evidence, its severity is a
judgment call with no shared scale, nobody can tell later whether it was
fixed or disputed, and `codev archive` accepts a change while a serious
defect is still open. The review roles now exist for every change, so their
output needs a durable, checkable home before it is relied on.

## What Changes

- A change may hold a **review record**, `_codev/changes/<name>/review.md`:
  one section per review step (`plan.challenge`, `code.review`), one
  subsection per role, and one finding per defect. Each finding has a stable
  id `R-<role-id>-<n>`, a title, a `severity` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) and
  a `confidence` (`high`, `low`) on scales defined once, a `location` (a
  file and lines of the project, or a heading of a planning artifact), a
  verbatim `evidence` quote, a `recommendation`, and an append-only
  `history` of statuses (`open`, `fixed`, `disputed`, `rejected`,
  `accepted-risk`, `deferred`), each entry naming who set it.
- A new read-only command **`codev review [--change <name>] [--json]`**
  shows the record: the findings by step and role with their current
  status, those waiting for an answer and from whom (the author, the
  reviewer, or a human), and the defects of the record itself.
- **`codev validate <change>`** checks an active change's record: format
  defects, duplicate ids, locations that do not exist, evidence that is not
  found verbatim at its location, a risk accepted or a `high` finding
  deferred by anyone but a human, and every `high` finding still
  unresolved. Each is an error, so the existing validation pre-flight makes
  **`codev archive` (and `codev sync`) refuse** a change with an unresolved
  `high` finding.
- The **`propose`** skill writes every `plan.challenge` finding to the
  record before fixing or reporting it, has the author answer and the
  reviewer re-check once, and builds its "Points to challenge" and a new
  "To decide" block from the record. The **`apply`** skill does the same at
  `code.review` for its "Review notes".
- Out of scope: running each reviewer as an isolated sub-agent, any
  configuration key for the review, and recording findings of
  `plan.trace`.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `review`

### Modified Capabilities

- `validation`
- `spec-merge`
- `changes`
- `skills`

### Removed Capabilities

## Impact

- `codev-core`: a pure parser and checker for the record format, and the
  derivation of each finding's current status and of who it waits for.
- `codev-engine`: reading the record and the files its locations cite,
  the new checks in `validate_change`, and the `review` use case.
- `codev-cli`: the `review` subcommand, its human rendering and a new
  `ReviewReportV1` in the JSON contract v1; shell completions follow the
  command list.
- `assets/workflows/propose.md` and `apply.md`: step 7 and step 5 write and
  read the record; regenerated skills through `codev update`.
- Documentation, in both `docs/en` and `docs/fr`: the review record and its
  scales (concepts and workflow chapters), the `codev review` command and
  the new validation codes in the reference.
- Existing changes are unaffected: a change without `review.md` gets no
  finding, and archived changes are never checked.

## Domains

<!-- No code diff yet (only planning files): ticked by judgement. -->

- [x] security — the record's `location` names files codev opens to check the evidence; a location must not let codev read outside the project
- [ ] personal-data — the record holds review findings and role ids, no personal data beyond the `human:<name>` an author chooses to write
- [ ] user-interface — a CLI command only, no graphical interface
- [ ] performance — one record per change, read only by `validate` and `review`
- [ ] operations — no service, no logs, no timeout involved
- [ ] migration — no existing change holds a record, so no change that archives today is refused tomorrow; no configuration or JSON field changes

## Release note

- Added: Review record per change. Reviewers' findings are written to `_codev/changes/<name>/review.md` with a stable id, a severity, a confidence, a verbatim quote of the evidence and a status history; `codev review` shows the record and what is waiting for an answer.
- Added: `codev validate` checks the review record, and `codev archive` refuses a change while a `high` finding is unresolved, until it is fixed or a person accepts or defers the risk.
- Changed: `/codev-propose` and `/codev-apply` record their review findings before fixing or reporting them, and list what only you can decide under "To decide".

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: The commands taking `--change` pick the change predictably

`codev status`, `codev instructions`, `codev review`, `codev sync` and
`codev archive` SHALL act on the change named by `--change` when it is
given. A name that is not a valid change name — the reserved `archive`
included — fails with `invalid_change_id`; a valid name with no folder
fails with `unknown_change`, whose message points to `codev list`. Without
`--change`:

- with exactly one active change, that change is used;
- with none, the command fails with `no_active_change` and the fix
  `create one with `codev new change <name>``;
- with several, the command fails with `ambiguous_change`, a message
  listing every active change, and a fix suggesting `--change` with the
  first one — it never picks one.

The archive folder is never an active change: it is never inferred nor
counted among the candidates.

A failure exits with code 1; with `--json`, the document keeps the
command's fields, set to `null` or empty, and carries the code in `status`.

#### Scenario: The single active change is inferred

- **GIVEN** one active change `add-auth`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the status of `add-auth` is shown

#### Scenario: The archive folder is not an active change

- **GIVEN** one active change `add-auth` and an archived change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the status of `add-auth` is shown

#### Scenario: No active change

- **GIVEN** a project without active change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status`
- **THEN** the command fails with `no_active_change` and the help names
  `codev new change`

#### Scenario: Several active changes

- **GIVEN** the active changes `add-auth` and `fix-bug`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1
- **AND** `status[0].code` is `ambiguous_change`, its message names
  `add-auth` and `fix-bug`, and `changeName` is `null`

#### Scenario: Several active changes for the review record

- **GIVEN** the active changes `add-auth` and `fix-bug`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1
- **AND** `status[0].code` is `ambiguous_change` and `changeName` is `null`

#### Scenario: A named change that does not exist

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --change ghost`
- **THEN** the command fails with `unknown_change` and a message naming
  `codev list`

#### Scenario: A named change with an invalid name

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions --change Bad`
- **THEN** the command fails with `invalid_change_id`

#### Scenario: The archive folder named as a change

- **GIVEN** a project with archived changes
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev status --change archive --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1
- **AND** `status[0].code` is `invalid_change_id`, its message says
  `archive` is reserved, and `changeName` is `null`

## Purpose

Keep what the reviewers of a change find in a durable record: each finding
identified, graded on shared scales, backed by verbatim evidence, and
followed through an append-only history of statuses, so that anyone can see
what is still open and who must answer it.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: A change's review record has a fixed format

A change MAY hold a review record, the file `review.md` at the root of its
folder. When present, the record SHALL be read as follows:

- its first line is `# Review record: <name>`, and it carries the format
  marker `<!-- codev-review: 1 -->`;
- each `## <step>` heading opens the section of a review step, `<step>`
  being one of the workflow steps that `codev roles` knows;
- each `### <role-id>` heading inside a step opens the section of a role;
- each `#### R-<role-id>-<n> <title>` heading inside a role's section opens
  a finding, where `<role-id>` is the role of the section, `<n>` a positive
  integer, and `<title>` a non-empty text; the heading is followed by one
  fenced `yaml` block holding the finding's fields;
- any other text — such as `No finding.`, `Disabled by configuration.` or a
  `Mode:` line — is free and carries no meaning for codev.

The fields of a finding SHALL be:

- `severity` (required) — `high`: the change would break a requirement,
  lose or expose data, or open a vulnerability, and must not be archived
  until it is fixed or a human accepts the risk; `medium`: a real defect or
  risk with a limited impact or a workaround; `low`: an improvement that
  does not decide whether the change is correct;
- `confidence` (required) — `high`: the evidence shows the problem
  directly; `low`: the problem depends on something the reviewer could not
  see or verify;
- `location` (required) — `<path>:<line>` or `<path>:<start>-<end>`, the
  path relative to the project root, for code; `<file>#<heading>`, the
  file relative to the change folder, for a planning artifact;
- `evidence` (required) — the text quoted from the location;
- `recommendation` (required) — what to do about it;
- `raised_by` (optional) — the list of the roles that raised the same
  defect, the section's role first;
- `history` (required, at least one entry) — the statuses of the finding,
  oldest first, each entry with `status` and `by`, and optionally `note`,
  `ref` and `to`.

A finding's id SHALL be unique in the whole record and SHALL never be
reused for another finding.

#### Scenario: A well-formed record is read

- **GIVEN** a change `add-auth` whose `review.md` holds the marker, a
  `## plan.challenge` section with a `### skeptic` section holding
  `#### R-skeptic-1 Session tokens never expire` and its `yaml` block with
  every required field
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** the document lists one finding `R-skeptic-1` under the step
  `plan.challenge` and the role `skeptic`, with its title, severity,
  confidence, location, evidence, recommendation and history
- **AND** `issues` is empty

#### Scenario: Free text between headings is ignored

- **GIVEN** a record whose `### security` section holds only the line
  `No finding.` and whose step section starts with `Mode: inline.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** no issue is reported for those lines
- **AND** the role `security` is listed with no finding

#### Scenario: A finding whose id does not match its role

- **GIVEN** a record with a heading `#### R-security-1 Weak hash` inside
  the `### skeptic` section
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** an issue `review_invalid` names the heading's line and says the
  id must start with `R-skeptic-`

#### Scenario: A missing required field

- **GIVEN** a finding whose `yaml` block has no `evidence` field
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** an issue `review_invalid` names the finding and the missing
  field `evidence`

### Requirement: A finding's status is the last entry of its history

A finding's history SHALL only grow: its current status is the `status`
of its last entry, among `open`, `fixed`, `disputed`, `rejected`,
`accepted-risk` and `deferred`. An entry `deferred` MUST carry `to` — the
change or the issue the finding goes to — and an entry `accepted-risk`
MUST carry `note` — the justification. The `by` of an entry SHALL be a
role id, `human`, or `human:<name>`.

A finding is **unresolved** while its current status is `open` or
`disputed`, and **resolved** otherwise.

A finding SHALL be **waiting for an answer** from:

- the `author` — when it is `open` and no entry yet comes from anyone but
  the roles that raised it;
- the `reviewer` — when its last entry is `fixed` or `disputed` and comes
  from someone other than the roles that raised it and a human;
- a `human` — when it is unresolved and none of the above applies: the
  author left it open, or the reviewer reopened it or maintained the
  dispute after the author answered.

A resolved finding waits for nobody.

#### Scenario: A new finding waits for its author

- **GIVEN** a finding `R-skeptic-1` whose history is one entry
  `status: open`, `by: skeptic`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** its `status` is `open` and its `waitingFor` is `author`

#### Scenario: A fix waits for the reviewer

- **GIVEN** the same finding with a second entry `status: fixed`,
  `by: architect`, `ref: design.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** its `status` is `fixed` and its `waitingFor` is `reviewer`

#### Scenario: A maintained dispute goes to a human

- **GIVEN** a finding whose history is `open` by `skeptic`, `disputed` by
  `architect`, then `disputed` by `skeptic`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** its `waitingFor` is `human`

#### Scenario: A verified fix waits for nobody

- **GIVEN** a finding whose last entry is `status: fixed`, `by: skeptic`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** its `waitingFor` is `null`

#### Scenario: A deferral without destination

- **GIVEN** a finding whose last entry is `status: deferred`,
  `by: human:Ludovic` and no `to`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** an issue `review_invalid` says a `deferred` entry needs `to`

#### Scenario: An unknown status

- **GIVEN** a finding with an entry `status: wontfix`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** an issue `review_invalid` names `wontfix` and lists the six
  statuses

### Requirement: `codev review` shows a change's review record

`codev review [--change <name>] [--json]` SHALL read the change's review
record and write nothing. It picks the change as the other commands taking
`--change` do.

The human output SHALL list, step by step and role by role in the record's
order, each finding on one line with its id, its severity, its confidence,
its current status, its title and its location, marking `(low confidence)`
the findings of confidence `low`, and `No finding.` for a role without
finding; then a **Waiting for an answer** block listing each finding that
waits, with its id and `author`, `reviewer` or `human`; then an **Issues in
the record** block listing each defect of the record with its line, its
code and its message — the same findings `codev validate` reports for the
record. An empty block SHALL say `None`.

With `--json`, the document SHALL carry `changeName`, `path` (the record's
path relative to the project root, or `null` when there is none), `steps`
— each with `step` and `roles`, each role with `id` and `findings`, each
finding with `id`, `title`, `severity`, `confidence`, `location`,
`evidence`, `recommendation`, `raisedBy`, `status`, `waitingFor` and
`history` — then `issues`, each with `code`, `severity`, `path`, `line` and
`message`, and `status` for execution errors.

A change without a record SHALL be reported as having no review record
yet, with an empty `steps` and `issues`. The command SHALL exit with code
`0` whenever it could read the change, whatever the record holds, and with
code `1` on an execution error.

#### Scenario: Human output of a record

- **GIVEN** a record with `R-skeptic-1` (`high`, `high`, `open`) and
  `R-security-1` (`medium`, `low`, `fixed` by `security`)
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** the output lists both findings under their step and role,
  `R-security-1` marked `(low confidence)`
- **AND** the **Waiting for an answer** block lists `R-skeptic-1` with
  `author`
- **AND** the **Issues in the record** block says `None`
- **AND** the exit code is 0

#### Scenario: A change without record

- **GIVEN** a change `add-auth` with no `review.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth --json`
- **THEN** `path` is `null`, `steps` and `issues` are empty and `status`
  is empty
- **AND** the exit code is 0

#### Scenario: Issues do not change the exit code

- **GIVEN** a record holding a finding with an unknown severity
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** the **Issues in the record** block lists a `review_invalid`
  issue with its line
- **AND** the exit code is 0

#### Scenario: The command writes nothing

- **GIVEN** a record with format defects
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change add-auth`
- **THEN** `review.md` and every other file of the project are unchanged

#### Scenario: An unknown change

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev review --change ghost --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1
- **AND** `status[0].code` is `unknown_change` and `changeName` is `null`

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The `propose` and `apply` skills keep their review findings in the record

At `plan.challenge` for the `propose` skill, and at `code.review` for the
`apply` skill, every finding a role raises SHALL be written to the change's
review record, under the step and the role, before it is fixed or
reported, with its evidence copied verbatim from the location it cites.
Before raising anything, the skill SHALL run
`codev review --change <name>`: a finding already in the record is never
raised again, and a finding already waiting for the author or the
reviewer is answered first.

Each finding still `open` SHALL then be answered once by the author — the
role that owns the cited artifact at `plan.challenge`, the `developer` at
`code.review` — by appending to its history: `fixed` with a `ref` when the
fix is unambiguous and within the change's scope, `disputed` with a `note`
pointing at the material that supports it, or left `open` when only a
person can decide. The finding's role SHALL then re-check each answer once:
a fix is verified (`fixed`) or reopened (`open`, with a `note`), a dispute
is accepted (`rejected`) or maintained (`disputed`, with a `note`). There is
no second round.

The skill MUST NOT write an `accepted-risk` entry, nor defer a `high`
finding, on its own: it lists them under **To decide**, and records the
person's decision — `by: human:<their git user name>`, or `by: human`
without one — only once the person has given it. A `medium` or `low`
finding MAY be deferred by its author, with `to`.

Before reporting, the skill SHALL run `codev review --change <name>` and
fix every issue it lists in the record itself — format, location,
evidence — never by changing what a finding says. Its summary is built
from the record: the findings not marked `(low confidence)` and not
`rejected`, and a **To decide** block listing every finding waiting for a
human and every `high` finding still unresolved, each with its id, what it
is, the author's argument, the reviewer's answer, and the choices — fix
it, accept the risk with a justification, or defer it to a change or an
issue — or "Nothing to decide" when there is none.

When no role is active at the step, the skill writes no record for it.

#### Scenario: A finding is recorded before it is fixed

- **GIVEN** a plan whose design cites a decision that does not exist
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` challenges the plan and fixes the design
- **THEN** `review.md` holds a finding under `plan.challenge` and the
  `skeptic`, whose history is `open` by `skeptic`, `fixed` by the
  `architect` with a `ref`, then `fixed` by `skeptic`
- **AND** `codev validate <name>` reports no `review_*` finding

#### Scenario: A resumed session does not raise a finding twice

- **GIVEN** a change whose record already holds `R-skeptic-1` under
  `plan.challenge`
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` challenges the plan again and finds the same
  defect
- **THEN** no new finding is added for it

#### Scenario: A high finding the author cannot settle goes to the person

- **GIVEN** a change whose proposal ticks `security`, and whose code stores
  a secret in clear text in a way only a product decision can change
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews the change
- **THEN** the record holds a `high` finding left `open` by the
  `developer`
- **AND** the summary's **To decide** block lists it with the choices fix,
  accept the risk, or defer
- **AND** the record holds no `accepted-risk` entry

#### Scenario: The person's decision is recorded

- **GIVEN** the same finding, and a person who answers "accept the risk:
  the secret is a test fixture", with `git config user.name` set to
  `Ludovic`
- **WHEN** the skill records the decision
- **THEN** the finding's last entry is `status: accepted-risk`,
  `by: human:Ludovic`, with that justification as `note`

#### Scenario: Nothing to decide

- **GIVEN** a review whose findings are all fixed and verified, or
  rejected
- **WHEN** the skill presents its summary
- **THEN** the **To decide** block says "Nothing to decide"

#### Scenario: A low-confidence finding is kept but not presented

- **GIVEN** a `medium` finding of confidence `low` that depends on a load
  the reviewer could not measure
- **WHEN** the skill presents its summary
- **THEN** the finding is in `review.md`
- **AND** it is not listed among the points or notes of the summary

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: The `propose` skill challenges the plan and reports points to challenge

After the traceability check, the `propose` skill SHALL re-read the
artifacts as reviewers who did not write them: every role
`codev roles --at plan.challenge --change <name> --json` returns — the
`skeptic` and the experts the change's domains activate — each along its
criteria, the project's extra criteria included, and using its
`knowledge` when it has one. The `skeptic`'s grid covers the need (does
the change solve the Why, is there a simpler solution or one without
code), the scope (anything nobody asked for, an obvious case missing), the
specs (error and edge cases, each requirement verifiable), the decisions
(a silent contradiction with a decision in effect), the assumptions (the
one that would bring the plan down if wrong) and the tasks (each one
verifiable). It MUST also apply, only when the proposal's Impact touches
them, the lenses security & privacy, compatibility & migration,
operability, performance, and accessibility & UX, as well as the project's
`rules:` received through `codev instructions`. An expert asks whether
the design addresses its domain.

Every finding of the pass MUST be written to the change's review record
and answered as the requirement on review findings describes. The pass
MUST fix what is unambiguous directly in the artifacts, and leave to a
person, under **To decide**, what needs a human decision. It MUST NOT add
scope.

The final summary of the skill MUST end with a "Points to challenge" block
built from the record's `plan.challenge` findings that are not marked
`(low confidence)` and not `rejected`: at most five items in total across
the roles, ranked by severity, each on one line tagged with the id of the
role that raised it and giving its finding id, its status, what, why it
matters and the artifact concerned. When the pass finds nothing worth
raising, the block MUST say "No point to challenge found" instead of
inventing points. A "To decide" block follows.

When no role is active at `plan.challenge`, the skill MUST skip the pass,
and the "Points to challenge" block MUST say that the skeptic is disabled
by configuration instead of listing points.

#### Scenario: Points to challenge are reported

- **GIVEN** a plan whose design rests on an unverified assumption
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` presents the plan
- **THEN** the summary contains a "Points to challenge" block naming the
  assumption, its finding id, why it matters and the artifact concerned,
  tagged `skeptic`
- **AND** the same point is recorded in `review.md` under
  `plan.challenge` and `skeptic`

#### Scenario: At most five points

- **GIVEN** a plan in which the skeptic finds four weak points and the
  `security` expert four more
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` presents the plan
- **THEN** the "Points to challenge" block lists at most five items in
  total, the most severe first, each tagged with its role id
- **AND** all eight findings are in `review.md`

#### Scenario: An active expert challenges the design

- **GIVEN** a change whose proposal ticks `personal-data` and whose design
  stores a new e-mail field with no retention rule
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` challenges the plan
- **THEN** the missing retention rule is fixed or raised as a point to
  challenge tagged `privacy`
- **AND** either way it is recorded in `review.md` under `privacy`

#### Scenario: Nothing to challenge

- **GIVEN** a plan in which the contrarian pass finds nothing worth raising
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` presents the plan
- **THEN** the summary says "No point to challenge found"
- **AND** lists no invented point

#### Scenario: A conditional lens outside the Impact is not applied

- **GIVEN** a plan whose Impact touches no user interface
- **WHEN** the contrarian pass runs
- **THEN** no accessibility & UX point is raised

#### Scenario: The pass does not add scope

- **GIVEN** a plan for which the reviewer thinks of a useful but unrequested
  feature
- **WHEN** the contrarian pass runs
- **THEN** the feature is not added to the artifacts

#### Scenario: The skeptic disabled by configuration

- **GIVEN** a configuration with `roles: { skeptic: never }` and a change
  that ticks no domain
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` presents the plan
- **THEN** no contrarian pass has run
- **AND** the "Points to challenge" block says the skeptic is disabled by
  configuration

#### Scenario: A project criterion joins the grid

- **GIVEN** a configuration where `skeptic` has the extra criterion
  `The rollback plan is stated`
- **WHEN** the contrarian pass runs on a plan with no rollback plan
- **THEN** the missing rollback plan is fixed or raised as a point to
  challenge

### Requirement: The `apply` skill reviews the change's code as a newcomer

Once every task is checked and before running the full test suite, the
`apply` skill SHALL re-read only the code the change added or modified,
with every role `codev roles --at code.review --change <name> --json`
returns — the `newcomer` and the experts the change's domains activate —
each along its criteria, the project's extra criteria included, and using
its `knowledge` when it has one. The `newcomer` reads as a developer
joining the project who has seen neither the plan nor the conversation:
each changed function makes sense without the plan or the conversation;
names say what things do, with no obscure abbreviation; a function too
long or too nested is split when it splits simply; dense one-liners,
premature genericity and single-use abstractions give way to the simple
version unless the clever one is justified; comments explain the why where
it is not obvious and never paraphrase the code; tests read as a
description of the behavior. It MUST also apply the project's `rules`
received through `codev instructions`. An expert asks whether the
implementation respects its domain.

Every finding of the review MUST be written to the change's review record
and answered as the requirement on review findings describes, the
`developer` being the author. The skill MUST simplify directly what is
unambiguous and re-run the affected tests. The review MUST NOT widen the
change's scope and MUST NOT modify code the change did not add or modify.
The `newcomer` MUST NOT change behavior. An expert MUST NOT change
behavior silently: a fix that changes behavior is reported as a note,
unless it is a clear defect within the change's scope, which is then fixed
with a test and named in the summary.

The final summary MUST carry a "Review notes" block built from the
record's `code.review` findings that are not marked `(low confidence)`
and not `rejected`, listing what the review did not fix alone: at most
five items in total across the roles, ranked by severity, each tagged with
the id of the role that raised it and giving its finding id, its status,
what, where and why. A `high` finding still unresolved MUST always be
listed, even beyond five. When the review finds nothing worth raising, the
block MUST say "No review concern found" instead of inventing notes. A
"To decide" block follows.

When no role is active at `code.review`, the skill MUST skip the review,
and the "Review notes" block MUST say that the review is disabled by
configuration.

#### Scenario: A needlessly clever construction is simplified

- **GIVEN** a change whose tasks are all checked, and whose code contains a
  dense one-liner with a simple equivalent
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews the change as a newcomer
- **THEN** the one-liner is replaced by the simple version
- **AND** the affected tests are run again and pass

#### Scenario: The review keeps behavior and scope

- **GIVEN** a change whose code could be simplified by also changing an edge
  case's behavior, or by adding an unrequested helper
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews the change as a newcomer
- **THEN** the behavior and the scope of the change stay as implemented
- **AND** the tests that passed before the review still pass

#### Scenario: At most five review notes

- **GIVEN** a review that finds seven concerns it does not fix alone, none
  of them of severity `high`
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` presents its final summary
- **THEN** the "Review notes" block lists at most five items, each tagged
  with its role id and giving its finding id, what, where and why
- **AND** all seven findings are in `review.md` under `code.review`

#### Scenario: A high-severity security finding is never dropped

- **GIVEN** a review with five readability notes and a `security` finding
  of severity `high` still `open`
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` presents its final summary
- **THEN** the `security` finding is listed in the "Review notes" block
- **AND** in the "To decide" block

#### Scenario: An expert reports a behavior-changing fix

- **GIVEN** a change whose proposal ticks `performance`, and whose code
  could be made faster by changing the order of its results
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews the change
- **THEN** the order of results is unchanged
- **AND** the suggestion appears as a review note tagged `performance`

#### Scenario: An expert fixes a clear defect within scope

- **GIVEN** a change whose proposal ticks `security`, and whose new
  endpoint builds an SQL query by concatenating a request parameter
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews the change
- **THEN** the query is parameterized, a test covers the hostile input,
  and the summary names the fix
- **AND** the record holds the finding, `fixed` by the `developer` with a
  `ref`, then `fixed` by `security`

#### Scenario: Nothing to note

- **GIVEN** a change whose code raises no review concern
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` presents its final summary
- **THEN** the summary says "No review concern found"
- **AND** lists no invented note

#### Scenario: Code outside the change is untouched

- **GIVEN** a change that calls an obscure function it did not modify
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews the change as a newcomer
- **THEN** that function is left unchanged
- **AND** it appears, at most, as a review note

#### Scenario: The review disabled by configuration

- **GIVEN** a change whose `change.yaml` holds `roles: { newcomer: never }`
  and whose proposal ticks no domain
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` has checked every task
- **THEN** no review runs and the full test suite runs next
- **AND** the "Review notes" block says the review is disabled by
  configuration

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Validation pre-flight before sync and archive

`codev sync` and `codev archive` MUST refuse to act if
`codev validate <change>` reports at least one error; they MUST do so
without performing the merge, without writing, and without moving anything,
and report the stable code `validation_failed`. The errors of the change's
review record count like any other, so a change with an unresolved `high`
finding is neither synced nor archived until it is fixed or a person
accepts or defers the risk.

#### Scenario: A change with a validation error is not archived

- **GIVEN** a change in which a delta has a `duplicate_requirement`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev archive <change>`
- **THEN** no main spec is modified
- **AND** the change remains active at its original location
- **AND** the error message names the code `validation_failed` and invites
  the user to run `codev validate <change>` to see the details

#### Scenario: A sync with a validation error merges nothing

- **GIVEN** a change containing a well-formed delta but also a requirement
  without `SHALL` (an error finding reported by validate)
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev sync --change <change>`
- **THEN** no main spec is modified
- **AND** the JSON error carries the code `validation_failed`

#### Scenario: An unresolved high finding blocks the archive

- **GIVEN** a well-formed change whose review record holds a `high`
  finding still `open`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev archive <change> --json`
- **THEN** no main spec is modified and the change remains active
- **AND** the JSON error carries the code `validation_failed`

#### Scenario: A risk accepted by a person no longer blocks

- **GIVEN** the same change after a last history entry
  `status: accepted-risk`, `by: human:Ludovic`, with a `note`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev archive <change>`
- **THEN** the change is archived, its `review.md` among its files

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The review record of an active change is checked

For each active change that holds a `review.md`, validation SHALL check the
record against the format the `review` capability describes and report, as
errors, each with the record's path and the line concerned:

- `review_invalid` — a format defect: the marker missing or of another
  version, a finding heading outside a role's section or a role's section
  outside a step, a step codev does not know, an id that does not match its
  role, a finding without a `yaml` block or with a block that is not valid
  YAML, a required field missing or empty, a severity, confidence or status
  outside its scale, a history with no entry, an entry without `by`, a
  `deferred` entry without `to`, an `accepted-risk` entry without `note`;
- `review_duplicate_id` — a finding id that appears more than once,
  naming every line where it appears;
- `review_location_not_found` — an unresolved finding whose location is
  not of either form, or does not name an existing
  file inside the project (or inside the change folder, for a planning
  artifact), lines beyond the end of that file, or a heading that the
  artifact does not hold;
- `review_evidence_not_found` — an unresolved finding whose evidence is not
  found verbatim within its location: within the cited lines for code,
  within the heading's section for a planning artifact; the comparison
  ignores line endings, the whitespace at the start and end of each line,
  and blank lines, and every other character counts;
- `review_decision_not_human` — an `accepted-risk` entry, or a `deferred`
  entry on a `high` finding, whose `by` is neither `human` nor
  `human:<name>`;
- `review_unresolved_high` — a `high` finding, whatever its confidence,
  whose current status is `open` or `disputed`, naming its id and saying
  that it must be fixed, or that a person must accept or defer the risk,
  before the change is archived.

A resolved finding's location and evidence SHALL NOT be checked: its fix
may have removed the quoted text, the lines or the file. Whatever its
status, a location MUST NOT make codev read a file outside the project. A change without `review.md` SHALL get no review
finding. Archived changes MUST NOT be checked: their history is not
rewritten.

#### Scenario: A clean record

- **GIVEN** an active change whose record holds a `high` finding fixed
  then verified by its role, and a `medium` finding `open` whose evidence
  is in the cited lines
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_*` finding is reported
- **AND** the exit code is 0

#### Scenario: An unresolved high finding

- **GIVEN** an active change whose record holds `R-security-1` of severity
  `high` whose last entry is `status: disputed`, `by: security`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_unresolved_high` error names `R-security-1` and its
  line
- **AND** the exit code is 1

#### Scenario: A high finding of low confidence still counts

- **GIVEN** an active change whose record holds a `high` finding of
  confidence `low`, still `open`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_unresolved_high` error is reported

#### Scenario: A risk accepted by a person

- **GIVEN** an active change whose record holds a `high` finding whose last
  entry is `status: accepted-risk`, `by: human:Ludovic`, with a `note`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_*` finding is reported

#### Scenario: A risk accepted by a role

- **GIVEN** an active change whose record holds a finding whose last entry
  is `status: accepted-risk`, `by: architect`, with a `note`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_decision_not_human` error names the finding and the
  entry's line

#### Scenario: A medium finding deferred by its author

- **GIVEN** an active change whose record holds a `medium` finding whose
  last entry is `status: deferred`, `by: developer`, `to: fix-cache`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_*` finding is reported

#### Scenario: Evidence that is not in the cited lines

- **GIVEN** an open finding located at `src/auth.rs:42-44` whose evidence
  is a line that `src/auth.rs` holds only at line 80
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_evidence_not_found` error names the finding and its
  location

#### Scenario: Evidence quoted with another indentation

- **GIVEN** an open finding whose evidence is the cited line without its
  leading spaces, on a project checked out with CRLF line endings
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_evidence_not_found` is reported

#### Scenario: Evidence of a fixed finding is not checked

- **GIVEN** a finding whose last entry is `status: fixed`, `by: security`,
  and whose evidence no longer appears in its file
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_evidence_not_found` is reported

#### Scenario: A fixed finding whose file was deleted

- **GIVEN** a finding whose last entry is `status: fixed`, `by: developer`,
  located in a file the fix deleted
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_location_not_found` is reported

#### Scenario: A plan location whose heading does not exist

- **GIVEN** an open finding located at
  `"design.md#Decision: Sessions live in the database"` in a change whose
  `design.md` holds no such heading
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_location_not_found` error names the heading

#### Scenario: A location outside the project

- **GIVEN** an open finding located at `../../etc/passwd:1`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_location_not_found` error is reported
- **AND** no file outside the project is read

#### Scenario: A duplicate id

- **GIVEN** a record holding `R-skeptic-2` under `plan.challenge` and again
  under `code.review`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a `review_duplicate_id` error names `R-skeptic-2` and both lines

#### Scenario: No record, no finding

- **GIVEN** an active change without `review.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no `review_*` finding is reported

#### Scenario: Archived records are not checked

- **GIVEN** a project whose only record with an unresolved `high` finding
  belongs to an archived change
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate`
- **THEN** no `review_*` finding is reported
